steps.say: One tripod position. Two fisheye lenses, back to back.
The practitioners' rule: don't solve poses on these. Stitch a panorama first.
steps.caption: two 200° circles, one camera position

scenes.headline: A 360 capture, posed five ways, checked against a scan
scenes.sub: One public room, a tripod, and a Faro LiDAR scan as the answer key
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nadir. I took one public 360 capture with a laser scan of the room, and tested that rule.

scenes.title: One ring of rays, three layouts

params.erp: Equirectangular: the ring smears sideways toward the pole
params.cube: Cube faces: round inside a face, stretched across an edge
params.fish: Dual fisheye: nearly even, out to the rim
params.seam: On the seam, the ring splits across both lenses

steps.term: ERP: the whole sphere as one 2:1 image
steps.say: Draw a small ring of directions and push it toward the ceiling. On the panorama it smears sideways.
Cut the sphere into cube faces and the ring stays round, until it crosses an edge.
On the two fisheye circles it stays round almost everywhere, except on the seam, where each lens sees half.
FIORD ships no panorama, so I stitched my own, and masked the seam in red.
It came out upside down. The frames are stored that way, and my tripod mask hid the ceiling.
steps.caption: the carpet is at the top

scenes.title: The thinned capture: every fourth position

states.say: Dense, every arm registered. So I thinned the capture to fourteen positions.

states.term: Rig: images known to share one centre
states.say: Loose cube faces fell apart. Three models, and not one position with all its faces together.
The panorama as one camera, or cube faces with the rig: all fourteen whole.
The surprise: the raw fisheye, with no rig at all, kept thirteen. Each lens sees past ninety degrees, so the two overlap.

scenes.label: how far apart a rigless cube position's face centres land
scenes.note: they should coincide; the rotations miss by 0.6°
scenes.say: Even dense, a rigless cube position's five faces land a median one point eight centimetres apart, and half a degree off.

params.units: SfM's cloud: no scale at all
params.height: the camera, 1.65 m above the floor
params.width: walls 6.73 m apart, in the scan
params.band: a scanned wall: 4 to 16 mm thick

steps.say: Structure from motion gives a shape with no size.
Fitted to the scan, the camera sits one point six five metres up. That's a tripod.
The scan's walls are six point seven three metres apart.
And each scanned wall is a band a few millimetres thick. That is the bar a splat has to meet.
A LiDAR scanner sells five millimetres.
But that is drift between targets, not the noise on one pipe.

scenes.text: Solve on the panorama or give the mapper the rig. Never hand it loose cube faces.
